evidence: CDIAL 9871 marate gives Punjabi marnā and Marwari marṇo “die”, but mar-gyo and mar-go contain a go light verb whose complete construction needs analysis.

CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem.

CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology.

CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed.
CDIAL 7136 nikaṭam explicitly gives Bshk. nīer and northwestern neṛe/neḍi/neḍḍhi “near”. The survey nīar/niḍe forms fit; initial m in mere remains a different comparison.
CDIAL 4721 calati gives the cal-/cāl- walk verb. The selected calā/cāllo forms are ordinary verbal inflections; initial h or zero needs local correspondence evidence.

CDIAL 2575 kaḥ punar gives kaun/koṇ/kuṇa “who” and Old Gujarati kuṇaïṃ instrumental. The q/k variants and final pronominal vowels preserve the family; Kalasha kura needs comparison with a different interrogative stem.
CDIAL 10158 mukha explicitly gives mouth/face mu/muh and retained-kh mukha forms. The simple survey moho/māī and mukh responses preserve these attested contractions or learned/regional forms.

CDIAL 986 asmad explicitly gives the ham/amh- and northwestern asī/asā we paradigms. Qualified inclusive/exclusive elicitation labels are preserved, without inventing a different root where the same documented form is used.

CDIAL 3083 kāla explicitly gives Bihari kariyā and Sindhi kāro “black”, with Western Pahari kāo. Survey ordinary vowel/gender variants retain this black adjective; karḍo/kaḍo needs separate extension analysis.
CDIAL 2757 kaphoṇi gives Hindi kohni/kehunī, Bengali kanui and Western Pahari khunni “elbow”. Simple contracted q/k and vowel variants preserve this historical elbow family.

CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions.

CDIAL 10234 mūtra explicitly gives Kalasha mūtra, Bshk. mūλ and Western Pahari mūc. The survey lateral/sibilant outcomes fit the tr-cluster urine family; retroflex muṭ and ordinary mute preserve the same noun, with phonetic details left open.
CDIAL 5301 jyotsnā explicitly gives Nepali jun and Assamese zon “moon”.

CDIAL 8857 prastara explicitly gives Prakrit patthara and regional pathar/pathara “stone”, including known cross-IA loans. Unaspirated patar remains a qualified phonetic variant within this identifiable stone family.
CDIAL 5086 jaṭā gives Bi. jar and Nepali jari/jaro “root”. Nasal-initial nar may be the separate nāḍī family; palatal/aspirated initial deviations need comparison before assigning.

CDIAL 9758 matsya explicitly gives Bshk. fish plural -cin and the eastern macharī -l/-r extension. Survey maśīn and macharī match those documented paradigmatic/extended forms, not the separate matsiya branch.

CDIAL 9349 bhaginī gives Bshk-area bai(n), Kashmiri biñ, Punjabi bhaiṇ and regional bahin/bheṇ “sister”. Simple n-retaining variants can be linked provisionally; additional r in baharṇ requires a separate morphological account.

CDIAL 6152 danta explicitly gives Maiya/Palula dān, Gawri dant and northwestern dand “tooth”; its addendum includes aspirated Sindhi dandh. The simple dān/dant/dandh survey forms therefore fit this family.

CDIAL 7733 pattra explicitly gives Lahnda pattar, Punjabi pattā and Bshk. paλ “leaf”. The l/ɬ notation in the latter and regional r-bearing or simple pata forms fit this branch; pana/pan may instead be parṇa.

CDIAL 10978 lavaṇa gives the widespread loṇ/lūṇ salt family. Regional retroflex initial ḷ and the northern retained-v lovn do not require a different lexical root; their phonetic details remain in the source transcription.

CDIAL 6495 dūra gives Palula dhūro and regional dūr “far”, with retroflex ḍūr in the addendum. The selected survey variants preserve the distance adjective; local r/ṛ articulation does not by itself establish another root.

CDIAL 4655.3 caturaḥ explicitly gives Bshk. čōr, Kalasha čāu, Khowar čhor, Maiya čōur and Palula čūr. These northern o/u forms require subsection 3, correcting the candidate’s subsection-2 link; western cār remains in subsection 2.

CDIAL 7655 pañca explicitly gives Dardic panž/panz and Pashai paĩ/paẽ, alongside Kalasha poñ and Shina poĩ. The survey affricate-to-sibilant and contracted nasal/glide numerals fit this documented five family; exact local phonetic developments remain qualified.

CDIAL 2668.2 kaṇṭaka explicitly gives Punjabi/Lahnda kaṇḍā, Palula kāṇḍu and Western Pahari kā̃ḍā “thorn”, with Garhwali kā̃ḍu in the addendum. These ending-bearing forms select kaṇṭaka, not bare kaṇṭa.
CDIAL 8265 putra explicitly gives northwestern puttar/puttur and Kashmiri pothar “son”. The r-retaining and ordinary vowel variants fit this family, with transmission and aspiration details retained.

CDIAL 4655.3 caturaḥ explicitly gives Bshk. čōr, Kalasha čāu, Khowar čhor, Maiya čōur and Palula čūr. These northern o/u forms require subsection 3, correcting the candidate’s subsection-2 link; western cār remains in subsection 2.

CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions.
CDIAL 5550 ḍimba explicitly gives Bengali ḍim and Assamese ḍimā “egg”.
